title: Rabbah bar Shimi (II)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Ravina’s student, as in Kiddushin 45b, where the Rabbis said to Ravina, “But perhaps…”; Rabbah bar Shimi said to them: “The Master said explicitly that he does not hold this of Rav,” etc. Rashi and Tosafot explain there in the name of the She’iltot, and Tosafot Rid, that he called Ravina “the Master.” Likewise in Pesachim 6b he speaks in Ravina’s name.

He is likewise mentioned in Megillah 24a after Rav Papa, giving the reason why the one who reads the haftarah from the Prophets leads the Shema: because they would come to quarrel. Hyman therefore considers Yuchasin correct in saying that there were two Rabbah bar Shimis, contrary to Seder HaDorot.

notes.text: Hyman attributes the Master identification to the named commentators and concludes that there were two homonyms. “After Rav Papa” can describe the sequence in the cited text; no extra generational inference is added.

Davidson Kiddushin 45b reads Rabbah bar Shimi’s explicit statement, and consulted Vilna Rashi explains Mar as Ravina. Tosafot/She’iltot/Tosafot Rid and Yuchasin/Seder HaDorot exact claims remain separately attributed. “After Rav Papa” does not alone establish a generation.
